result.title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Recent work has sought to localize the internal mechanisms underlying visual reasoning skills in vision-language models. These methods largely overlook separability and composability in both mechanism identification and evaluation. We propose separability and composability as two important desiderata for skill localization. Separability requires identified mechanisms to contribute primarily to their target skills while having limited effects on other skills, enabling precise diagnosis and targeted intervention. Composability requires skill mechanisms to be combinable to support complex tasks, allowing a small set of mechanisms to account for broader capabilities. In this work, we propose a multi-skill interpretability framework DISCO, built around these two properties. For identification, we propose Separable Head Selection, which selects skill-specific attention heads based on their contributions across skills. For evaluation, we are the first to design metrics for measuring separability and composability of identified heads. Extensive experiments on three VLMs and four fundamental visual reasoning skills demonstrate the effectiveness of DISCO. It achieves the highest separability, outperforming the strongest baseline by 24.80, 18.38, and 13.75 points across the three models, respectively, while also achieving the highest composability on all three models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「可分性」与「可组合性」两项技能定位原则，并给出多技能可解释框架 DISCO：用跨技能贡献挑选技能专属注意力头，并首次设计度量来评估这些头的可分性与可组合性，在三个 VLM 和四类视觉推理技能上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接研究 VLM 视觉推理技能在内部注意力头上的定位与跨技能干扰，其可分性、可组合性度量可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与多假设 latent 的贡献分配和技能叠加方式，但未涉及推理期 latent 状态生成。
